text: dsh-compact-receipt 是面向 DSH 会话的上下文压缩插件：它监听用户消息和压缩摘要，记录约束、决策与验收要求，并在每次压缩后生成收据，列出摘要中可能缺失的要求及存活情况。用户可用 /contract 查看最近收据和仍有效的要求，也可查看探针结果、管理写入保护；保护会依据已记录的禁止要求拦截匹配路径的写入工具调用。可选的引擎模式会把有效要求附加到摘要。

dsh-compact-receipt tracks requirements across DSH compactions. After compaction, it creates a receipt showing which recorded requirements may be missing. Use /contract to view receipts, inspect a probe, or manage the write guard. Optional engine mode appends active requirements to summaries.
想知道 DSH 压缩上下文时有没有把我之前提的要求弄丢。
让 DSH 在压缩后给我一份要求存活情况的收据。
Show me which project constraints may have disappeared after a DSH context compaction.
dsh-compact-receipt 的功能「压缩收据」：压缩摘要生成后，它将此前记录的要求与摘要比较，并通过 /contract 展示存活、疑似丢失及未能判断的项目；若有疑似丢失项，还会把提示注入会话。
dsh-compact-receipt 的功能「写入保护」：记录禁止要求后，插件检查写入工具的目标路径并拦截匹配项；可用 /contract guard off 关闭，或用 /contract unblock <id> 解除规则。
dsh-compact-receipt 使用前须知：启用可用的 DSH 模型路由时，语义分类和判定会把部分历史用户消息、要求及压缩摘要发给当前配置的模型服务；代码未固定服务商或要求插件专属密钥。

dsh-compact-receipt README · dsh-compact-receipt：> ## ⚠️ Beta (0.4.0-beta.1)
>
> **A default install is safe**: it records, audits and guards; it does not change compaction.
>
> **The compaction takeover is experimental and has not been exercised by a real compaction yet.**
> Two end-to-end runs never triggered compaction (likely `auto` not enabled or a threshold floor),
> so the pinned block has never been produced in a live session - only unit-tested.
>
> The takeover is off by default and requires both `engine: true` and disabling the `compaction-basic`
> row. Until a real compaction verifies it, **do not use it on important sessions**.

dsh-compact-receipt README · dsh-compact-receipt：[中文](README.zh.md) | English

> Long conversations don't forget. Nobody tells you when they started.

Context compaction in DSH is **silent and lossy**: a range of history is replaced by one summary,
and from then on that summary is all the model can see. The "don't touch tests/" you said 40 turns
ago may have vanished in a compaction — with nothing to indicate it.

dsh-compact-receipt README · dsh-compact-receipt：This plugin hands you a **receipt** after every compaction: how much was eaten, and which of your
requirements no longer appear in the summary.

```
This session compacted 1 time, most recent:

Receipt #1 · 18:42:07 · ate 24 history items (~8.2k tokens)
  5 commitments · 4 survived · 1 possibly lost

dsh-compact-receipt README · Not another context dashboard：Existing tools measure **how big** the context is (`dsh-context`) or make it **smaller** (`billion-context`).
This one measures a different thing: after compaction, **are the things you asked for still there?**

dsh-compact-receipt README · Not another context dashboard：- Others optimize token count; this audits semantic fidelity
- Others ask you to pin a passage by hand (`dsh-highlightpin`); this is automatic and zero-config
- The audit **never calls a model**: the summary is a string, your requirements are strings, so the
  comparison is string comparison — **zero token cost**, cheap enough to run on every compaction

dsh-compact-receipt README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:cty-09/dsh-compact-receipt
```

Restart DSH. No configuration, no toggles.

dsh-compact-receipt README · Usage：| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `/contract` | Latest receipt, commitments still in force, lifetime survival rate |
| `/contract guard off` | Disable blocking (on by default) |
| `/contract unblock <id>` | Lift one rule |

dsh-compact-receipt README · Architecture (v0.3)：- **Semantic classification**: one batched call over the shadowed messages adds the phrasings the rules
  miss ("tests 目录先别碰") to the commitment table - this is what moves coverage from rules to the model.
- **Semantic judgement**: commitments plus the new summary go to the model in one call that
  returns kept/lost/unclear. If it cannot answer, the rule scorer runs and the receipt says so.
- **Delivery is verified**: an injected message echoes back as a `user/message` event; the receipt
  only claims "confirmed delivered" when that echo arrives. A successful write is not delivery.
- **Classification probe**: `/contract probe` measures what a pinned policy would keep and how much
  context it would cost, without changing anything.
- **Rule-layer accuracy is measured, not asserted**: `test/corpus.js` holds 21 labelled messages and
  `npm test` prints the score. Today the rules reach **86%** (100% precision on constraints, decisions
  and acceptance; 70% constraint recall) - postposed negations like "tests 目录先别碰" are the misses,
  and the semantic layer covers them.

dsh-compact-receipt README · It also does two more things：**1. It tells you inside the conversation.** When a compaction drops requirements, a receipt card appears
in the chat — visible in the Web UI without remembering any command. That card also hands the dropped
requirements back to the model, so it is both an alert and the cheapest possible repair.

dsh-compact-receipt README · It also does two more things：**2. It blocks contradicting writes.** Once "don't touch X" is recorded, a write-family tool call targeting
`X` is denied, with a message telling the agent to confirm with you first, or you to run
`/contract unblock <id>`. Only file-writing tools are covered, and matching is path-string based:
missing a block is preferable to a false block.
section: It also does two more things

text:
dsh-compact-receipt README · What counts as a requirement：Three kinds, matched by rules (Chinese and English):

| Kind | Examples |
|---|---|
| constraint | don't touch X, must use Y, 不要改 X, 必须用 Y |
| decision | we'll use X, 决定采用 Y |
| acceptance | acceptance: tests must pass, 验收标准是 X |

Extraction is deterministic: same input, same output. No cost, no network, reproducible.

dsh-compact-receipt README · Honest limits：1. **"Possibly lost" means possibly.** A summary that keeps the meaning but rewords it can trigger a
   false alarm. The threshold deliberately prefers false alarms over silence.
2. **Only the compacted range is audited.** Requirements still in context are not audited, because
   they were never dropped.
3. **Rule extraction misses things.** It recognizes common imperative phrasing and nothing else. It
   does not guess.
4. **It does not prevent compaction and cannot restore the original text.** It makes the loss visible and
   puts the dropped requirements back in front of the model.
5. **Blocking is path-string matching.** Only file-writing tool arguments are inspected; a different spelling
   of the same path (symlink, relative form) can slip through.
6. **No dedicated sidebar panel.** A client plugin needs the custom `window.__ModuleLoader__` bundle
   format, `ctx.slots`, and a React build; this version does not ship one. Visibility comes from the
   in-conversation card and `/contract`.
7. **It does not take over the compactor.** Replacing `CompactionEngine` means reimplementing
   summarisation, range selection and checkpoint writes

dsh-compact-receipt README · How it works：DSH writes a `compaction/summary` event carrying the summary text and the seqs of shadowed history.
The plugin subscribes to the session event stream, extracts commitments from user messages as they
arrive, and on compaction scores each one against the summary text: exact match for Latin
identifiers, character-bigram overlap for Chinese, averaged. No model calls, no network, no extra tokens.

dsh-compact-receipt README · Development：```sh
npm test    # 20 cases, including an end-to-end simulation
```

Zero dependencies, zero build step: the ESM in `lib/` is the published artifact.

> Why no imports at all: `@deepseek-ai/*` runtime packages exist only inside the DSH install,
> not in a profile, and DSH registers no ESM resolve hook. Any third-party plugin that imports them
> fails with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` on a user's machine. This plugin therefore uses `ctx` only.
